author: fxfury
text:
PureMuscle wrote: Thanks guys - will do:)

Having looked at the training article on supply and demand, and now coupling it with this RBD concept, would you guys say that it's more appropriate to look at levels of support and resistance as general zones instead of a specific price level, for example 1.2000 to 1.2020 as a zone instead of 1.2000 as a precise level? The season I would ask, is that how would one decide on where exactly to trade once price enters a zone? With a price level, you'd know, or at least think you know

where to enter.

It is definitely about identifying zones to trade from and where price has decided to be too expensive or too cheap. Also 1.2000 would be considered a Big Round Number (BRN) and is something you should definitely be aware of because we expect reactions around these psychological levels.

I highly suggest reading emenes, blog and going to ken's pdf that is linked in his latest post, you will definitely understand a zone.

author: Rufus
text:
Hey Simple!!!

Good to see you over here. I know "Sandy" is coming through so brace yourself. Sounds like she is quite cranky.

S/D levels are looking good to me. One thing you will see as you draw these buggers out is which ones fail or produce a profit. This will also give you an indication of what potentially strong zones look like before price returns to them. To me how price leaves a zone is the way I judge it the most. Another is when the zone was formed and when price returns.

In general week zone formation and leaving make for week moves when price returns.

Take care Simple. If "IF" has something to add I am sure he will. I know he is busier then a three peckered billy goat trying to answer all the questions and homework.

Anyway button down the hatches
